ledger: Collage Studio — Wall of Wishes. APPEND-ONLY public credit ledger: every capability built from a wish credits the person who wished it, permanently. The immutability IS git history — this file is committed to a public repo, hash-chained, forked, and archived, so a credit can never be quietly erased. NEVER rewrite or remove an entry; only append. Anonymous wishers are credited as 'an anonymous Collage user'. Isomorphed from av/credits.json, which proved the pattern first.

credits.where: Settings panel — Arrangement and Crop focus, and both are rolled by the dice
credits.wish: More unique algorithms and sorting capabilities like the color match. Also maybe twisting capabilities or cropping algorithms for what to center on. Anything arrangement and composition wise to create more variation in the dice
credits.shipped_note: Shipped: 11 arrangements (photo metric x fragment spatial key, zipped — not a list sort) and 5 crop-focus modes, both rolled by the dice and carried in the share code. NOT yet shipped from this wish: 'twisting' (per-fragment rotation), which needs the draw loop in stage.ts plus both export paths and is its own increment.

credits.where: Settings panel — Twist, and it is rolled by the dice
credits.wish: More unique algorithms and sorting capabilities like the color match. Also maybe twisting capabilities or cropping algorithms for what to center on. Anything arrangement and composition wise to create more variation in the dice
credits.shipped_note: The 'twisting' half of the same wish, finished. 5 modes (Straight, Tilt, Scatter, Pinwheel, Cascade), rolled by the dice and carried in the share code. The fragments TILE the canvas, so nothing rotates a cell — the clip path stays exactly where it was and the SAMPLING inside it leans, with the destination grown by |cos|+|sin| so the corners cannot open up. Reaches all four render paths (live Stage, static preview, raster export, SVG export) through the one geometry function they already share.

credits.capability: A video just loads and loops — nothing asks about frames
credits.where: Anywhere you add a video, and Settings > the line where the frame switch used to be
credits.wish: You're still asking for how many frames to pull instead of just loading the video. Stop asking for frames period.
credits.shipped_note: The third filing of this complaint, and the first one that changed the surfaces the wisher was actually looking at. The frame-picker route is DELETED, not defaulted off: no sheet, no queue, no genart.framePicker preference (a stale '1' had been pinning returning users to it), no Settings switch, and the button that takes a video no longer calls itself 'Extract frames from a video'. The intake also stopped making you wait for the frame it was pulling: probe + re-open + prime + three seeks became one openClip() pass with one seek, 3,517ms -> 490ms to the clip reaching the collage.

credits.capability: Hi-res video export — the size ladder, drawn from your originals
credits.where: Export sheet > Video > Size — long edge (appears when a clip is on the canvas)
credits.wish: Would be nice to have same hi res output feature like the photo or a simple way to do full screen and capture data to a zip that can be preserved and loaded later,
credits.shipped_note: The first clause, and it was two stacked ceilings rather than a missing dropdown. SIZE: the Stage's maxBackingWidth was never passed, so it fell back to the 1200 logical width and EVERY exported MP4 was 1200px wide on every device, from any source, while the still export offered 16384. SOURCE: the Stage draws previewSrc, the <=1024px thumbnail — the still exporter draws the ORIGINAL and documents that exact asymmetry as a bug it already fixed; the video path never got it. Shipping the size alone would have been a bigger container of upscaled thumbnails, so both moved together: measured at one canvas size, detail energy went 33.0 -> 124.4 (3.8x). End to end on a real take: 1200x1802 -> 2488x3732. Rungs are PROBED per device AND per composition shape (H.264 caps the frame in macroblocks, so the ceiling depends on the aspect) and a rung the encoder refuses is shown unavailable with the real reason rather than offered and failed later. The full-res decodes are budgeted by geometry — each original is rasterised only to the pixels its own fragments consume and released immediately — because holding a pool of originals resident is a dead tab on a phone. ALREADY SERVED, verified on the running app rather than assumed: 'full screen' is the F key / the Maximize button (full bleed, Esc to leave), and the .collage archive already saves and reopens your sources and every setting. Video clips still are not carried in that archive.

credits.capability: Crash-safe autosave — your work survives a reload, and the app offers it back
credits.where: Automatic (IndexedDB, on every edit) + the restore banner at the top of the next launch
credits.wish: As I was capturing the video at 4k resolution — the app refreshed or crashed and lost what I was doing
credits.shipped_note: A 4K capture pushed the phone's browser over its memory line, the tab reloaded, and the whole collage was gone — because every bit of project state lived only in React state and NOTHING was ever autosaved; the only durable save was manually downloading a .collage, which nobody does mid-capture. Now the working project is written to IndexedDB continuously (debounced ~1.5s) with an IMMEDIATE checkpoint the instant an export or capture begins — the exact moment that crashes — and the next launch offers 'pick up where you left off', restoring your images and every setting. Built on the proven .collage round-trip (buildProjectBlob extracted from the manual save; restore = loadProject on the stored blob through the same hydration path Open uses), so there is one format and no drift; the archive never zips video, so autosaving stays cheap beside a heavy capture. A beforeunload guard also warns before an accidental refresh, and IndexedDB failing (private-mode Safari) can never break the editor. NOT yet carried into the session: the soundtrack and live video clips — a restored video project comes back as its stills plus every setting, the same limitation the manual .collage archive has, and the next rung.
